title: Functional-parity evidence record
description: One record is the functional-parity evidence for one REFACTOR work item: it fixes the observable contract asserted unchanged, the baseline observed before the change, the post-change evidence observed after it, the neutral evidence kinds relied on with the limitations of each, the explicit gaps, and a per-assertion and overall VERIFIED / UNVERIFIED verdict. `records` is non-empty: a functional-parity document with no record proves nothing. The record carries the form and the semantic requirements only; it never carries a product's test runner, snapshot framework, commands, configuration or test paths, which are Instance/repository data (verification/functional-parity/functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §8). No evidence kind is marked mandatory, primary or default: the `kind` enum is an unordered set of neutral kinds, `public-contract-snapshot` is one member of it and is the only kind that requires an applicability justification. This schema checks structure; the inference rules a schema of this subset cannot express, because they relate one part of a record to another, are enforced by the `functional-parity` check in scripts/kernel-validate.mjs against the fixtures beside this file and re-stated for review in functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §7 and §9: (1) the document carries at least one record; (2) every preserved-contract assertion id is unique across the whole record, the four facets included, and it maps to exactly one owning facet; (3) every per-assertion verdict names a declared assertion, and every declared assertion carries exactly one per-assertion verdict; (4) every evidence `covers` id resolves to a declared assertion, and every post-change `contract_links` entry resolves to the exact {facet, assertion_id} pair of a declared assertion — a right id under the wrong facet is rejected; (5) a per-assertion VERIFIED requires BOTH at least one evidence entry that covers the assertion AND at least one post-change contract link that resolves to it — evidence `covers` alone is not sufficient, and `contract_links` may be empty only when no assertion is VERIFIED; (6) `relationship: same` means the post-change observation reproduced exactly the baseline's identified conditions, every one of them and no others, referenced by id, with no duplicate baseline condition id — the word in a description is not evidence of it; (7) any UNVERIFIED per-assertion state forces an UNVERIFIED overall; (8) a record-scoped gap forces every declared per-assertion verdict UNVERIFIED and the overall UNVERIFIED; an assertion-scoped gap forces only the assertions it names, leaving the rest free to stand; (9) a baseline whose provenance is not established forces every declared per-assertion verdict UNVERIFIED and the overall UNVERIFIED, regardless of any gap; (10) the baseline and the post-change source states are a distinguishable pair — the same {identifier_kind, identifier} for both is not a before/after comparison.

records.description: One record per REFACTOR work item whose functional parity is being evidenced. Non-empty: an evidence document with no record proves nothing.

assertion.description: One statement of what stays observably identical across the change. `id` is referenced by evidence entries, by post-change contract links and by the per-assertion verdict. It is unique across the whole record — the four facets included — and the facet it is declared under is its one owning facet; the `functional-parity` check rejects a repeated id and resolves every reference to the exact {facet, id} pair.

facet.description: One facet of the preserved observable contract. Either it carries at least one assertion, or it carries a justification for why the facet does not apply to this work item — a facet may not simply be left blank, because a missing facet is a gap, not a pass (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §2, §7).

state_ref.description: An identifiable state of the source. `identifier_kind` names what kind of identifier `identifier` is (a revision, a tag, a build id, a described environment state) in neutral terms; the concrete scheme is repository data. The baseline's state_ref and the post-change state_ref identify the state before and after the change: the `functional-parity` check rejects an identical {identifier_kind, identifier} pair for both, because that is not a before/after comparison. The same `identifier` string under a different `identifier_kind` is a different pair and is not rejected on that ground.

identified_condition.description: One baseline input or observation condition, carrying a stable `id` that the post-change observation references when it claims to have reproduced the same conditions. Ids are unique within the baseline; the `functional-parity` check rejects a repeat.

condition.description: One post-change input or observation condition, restated in full because it is not identical to a baseline condition. Used only when `relationship` is `explicitly-comparable`.

observed_result.description: The result actually observed — not the result expected. An empty summary is not an observation.

evidence_entry.description: One neutral piece of evidence. `observed_scope` states exactly what this piece observed, so that a narrow piece is not read as a broad one. `covers` lists the assertion ids it supports; it does not on its own make an assertion VERIFIED — that also needs a post-change contract link (record rule 5). `limitations` is required and non-empty: every kind has limits, and an unlisted limitation is treated as an unnamed one. `applicability_justification` is required only for `public-contract-snapshot`; it is permitted on any kind but demanded of none of the others, so that no kind becomes the default by being the cheapest to record.

kind.description: Unordered set of neutral evidence kinds. behavioral-assertion: an automated assertion exercising the observable behaviour on the same inputs before and after. observation-log: a recorded observation of the running unit under stated conditions. interface-enumeration: an enumeration or diff of the declared public surface. interaction-trace: a recorded trace of outward interactions and side effects. public-contract-snapshot: a captured snapshot of the public contract compared before and after — one kind among these, never the default (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §6). differential-execution: the same inputs run through the old and the new implementation with the results compared.

gap.description: An explicit gap in the evidence: an incomplete baseline, non-comparable conditions, a missing observable facet, incomplete post-change evidence or an unjustified evidence kind. `scope` says how far the gap reaches. `record`: every declared per-assertion verdict is UNVERIFIED and the overall is UNVERIFIED (record rule 8) — a record-scoped gap does not leave any assertion standing. `assertion` (with `assertion_ids`): only the assertions it names are forced UNVERIFIED; an assertion the gap does not name is free to be VERIFIED on its own evidence. A gap never coexists with a VERIFIED verdict on what it affects.

work_item.description: Identifier of the REFACTOR work item this record is the functional-parity evidence for. Neutral: a work-item id, not a product ticket URL.

preserved_contract.description: The observable contract asserted unchanged, across all four facets. Every facet is present — a facet that does not apply carries a justification, it is not omitted (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §2). Assertion ids are unique across all four facets together.

baseline.description: The observation made before the change (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §3). Each input/condition carries a stable id so the post-change observation can reference it. `source_state` identifies the state before the change and must be a distinguishable pair from the post-change `source_state` (record rule 10).

provenance.description: How the baseline observation was obtained and whether that was actually established. `established: false` is a gap, not a pass: it forces every declared per-assertion verdict UNVERIFIED and the overall UNVERIFIED (record rule 9).

post_change_evidence.description: The observation made after the change, on the same or explicitly comparable inputs and conditions, tied to specific preserved-contract assertions (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §4). `source_state` identifies the state after the change and must be a distinguishable pair from the baseline `source_state` (record rule 10).

inputs_and_conditions.description: `relationship: same` — the post-change observation reproduced exactly the baseline's identified conditions: it carries `baseline_condition_ids` referencing them, every one of the baseline's ids and no others, and carries neither `items` nor a justification. `relationship: explicitly-comparable` — the conditions differ: it carries `items` restating them in full and a `comparability_justification`, and no `baseline_condition_ids`. There is no third value; conditions that are neither are a gap.

contract_links.description: The field is always present; the array may be empty only when no per-assertion verdict is VERIFIED — a record where every assertion is honestly UNVERIFIED needs no link. Each entry ties this post-change observation to one preserved-contract assertion by its exact owning facet and id. The `functional-parity` check resolves every entry to a declared {facet, assertion_id} pair: a right id under the wrong facet is rejected. A per-assertion VERIFIED requires at least one entry here that resolves to it; evidence `covers` alone is not enough. Narrow evidence is not silently widened: an observation may only claim the assertions it names here.

gaps.description: Explicit gaps. An empty array is a positive claim that none of the listed gap classes apply, not an absence of the field.

verdict.description: Per-assertion and overall verdict. Every declared assertion carries exactly one per-assertion entry. A per-assertion VERIFIED is legitimate only when the assertion is declared, the baseline provenance is established, at least one evidence entry covers it, and at least one post-change contract link resolves to its exact {facet, id} pair; an UNVERIFIED assertion needs its reason but no link, provided a gap or the reason records the missing observation. An overall VERIFIED is legitimate only when every per-assertion entry is VERIFIED and no record-scoped gap is present (functional-parity-evidence-contract.md §9).
